title: Lab 407 - Ansible Roles

lab_objective.description: By performing this lab, you will learn how to create, organize, and use Ansible roles to manage configurations in a structured and reusable way.
objectives: Understand the concept and purpose of Ansible roles.
Understand the standard directory structure of an Ansible role.
Create an Ansible role using the ansible-galaxy init command.
Understand the purpose of tasks, handlers, defaults, vars, and templates directories.
Define and use variables within an Ansible role.
Create tasks to install and configure Nginx.
Use handlers and notify directives within a role.
Create and use a Jinja2 template to configure a web page.
Execute an Ansible role through a separate playbook.
Understand how roles help organize and reuse automation code.
scenario: You are an Ansible administrator responsible for configuring an Nginx web server on a managed node in the dev host group.

Your task is to create an Ansible role named nginx_setup that installs Nginx, starts and enables its service, creates a custom web page using a Jinja2 template, and configures the firewall to allow HTTP traffic.
You must organize the configuration using the standard Ansible role directory structure and execute the role through a separate playbook.

tasks.title: Create an Ansible Role
steps: Log in to the Ansible control node as the srvc user.
Navigate to the srvc user's home directory.
Create an ~/ansible/roles directory if it does not already exist.
Navigate to the roles directory.
Use the ansible-galaxy init command to create a role named nginx_setup.
Explore the directory structure created by the command.
Identify the purpose of the following directories: tasks, handlers, defaults, vars, templates, files, and meta.

tasks.title: Understand the Role Directory Structure
steps: Navigate to the nginx_setup role directory.
Explore the files created inside each directory.
Identify the main.yml file inside the tasks directory.
Identify the main.yml file inside the handlers directory.
Identify the main.yml file inside the defaults directory.
Identify the main.yml file inside the vars directory.
Understand that the tasks directory contains the main tasks executed by the role.
Understand that the handlers directory contains handlers triggered by notify directives.
Understand that the defaults directory contains default variable values.
Understand that the vars directory contains role variables with higher precedence than role defaults.
Understand that the templates directory stores Jinja2 templates.

tasks.title: Define Default Variables
steps: Navigate to the defaults directory inside the nginx_setup role.
Open the main.yml file.
Define the following variables:
nginx_package: nginx
nginx_service: nginx
firewall_service: firewalld
http_port: 80/tcp
nginx_root: /usr/share/nginx/html
nginx_page: /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html
Save the file.
These variables will be used by the role tasks instead of repeating literal values.

tasks.title: Create Tasks to Install Nginx
steps: Navigate to the tasks directory inside the nginx_setup role.
Open the main.yml file.
Create a task to install the Nginx package using the package module.
Use the nginx_package variable to specify the package name.
Create another task to start the Nginx service and enable it at boot.
Use the nginx_service variable to specify the service name.
Use the service module to manage the service.

tasks.title: Start and Enable Firewalld
steps: In the tasks/main.yml file, create a task to start the firewalld service and enable it at boot.
Use the firewall_service variable to specify the service name.
Use the service module to manage firewalld.
Ensure the task is executed with the required administrative privileges through the main playbook.

tasks.title: Create the Web Document Root
steps: Create a task to ensure that the directory specified by nginx_root exists.
Use the file module.
Set the directory state to directory.
Use the nginx_root variable for the directory path.

tasks.title: Create and Deploy a Static File Using Copy
steps: Navigate to the files directory inside the nginx_setup role.
Create a file named welcome.txt.
Add the following content to the file:
Welcome to LINOOP Ansible Training!
Managed Host: {{ ansible_fqdn }}
IP Address: {{ ansible_default_ipv4.address }}
This file was deployed using the Ansible copy module.
Save the file.
Return to the tasks/main.yml file.
Create a task to copy welcome.txt from the role's files directory to /usr/share/nginx/html/welcome.txt on the managed node.
Use the copy module.
Ensure the file is copied with the correct content.

tasks.title: Create a Jinja2 Web Page Template
steps: Navigate to the templates directory inside the nginx_setup role.
Create a file named index.html.j2.
Add the following HTML and Jinja2 content to templates/index.html.j2:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
Welcome to LINOOP Ansible Training!
Managed Host: {{ ansible_fqdn }}
IP Address: {{ ansible_default_ipv4.address }}
This file was deployed using the Ansible template module.
</body>
</html>
Save the template.

tasks.title: Deploy the Dynamic Web Page Using a Template
steps: Return to the tasks/main.yml file.
Create a task to deploy the index.html.j2 template to the managed node.
Use the template module.
Set the destination to the file specified by nginx_page.
Ensure that Jinja2 variables are replaced with their actual values before the file is deployed.
Ensure the template is deployed to the Nginx document root.

tasks.title: Configure the Firewall
steps: Create a task to allow HTTP traffic through firewalld.
Use the ansible.posix.firewalld module.
Use the http_port variable to specify the port.
Make the firewall rule permanent.
Set the rule state to enabled.
Use notify to trigger a handler named Reload firewalld whenever the firewall configuration changes.

tasks.title: Create a Handler
steps: Navigate to the handlers directory inside the nginx_setup role.
Open the main.yml file.
Create a handler named Reload firewalld.
Use the service module to reload the firewalld service.
Use the firewall_service variable for the service name.
Ensure the handler is triggered by the notify directive in the firewall task.

tasks.title: Create a Main Playbook
steps: Navigate to the roles directory, outside the nginx_setup role directory.
Create a playbook named lab407_roles.yml.
Target the dev host group using hosts: dev.
Set gather_facts to true.
Use become: true to execute administrative tasks with elevated privileges.
Add a roles section to the playbook.
Include the nginx_setup role under the roles section.
Save the playbook.

tasks.title: Execute and Validate the Role
steps: Check the playbook syntax using ansible-playbook --syntax-check.
Execute the playbook against the dev host group.
Verify that Nginx is installed.
Verify that the Nginx service is running and enabled at boot.
Verify that the custom web page exists at the configured document root.
Verify that the web page contains the expected title and managed host information.
Verify that the firewall allows TCP port 80.
Execute the playbook a second time without making changes.
Observe the task results and confirm that Ansible reports changed: 0 when the configuration is already in the desired state.

completion_message: Lab 407 completed successfully! You have created an Ansible role using the standard directory structure, organized tasks, handlers, default variables, and Jinja2 templates, and executed the role through a separate playbook to configure an Nginx web server.
